answer: [NIKA] Identity minting requires a berth: the registry auctions a capped number of slots per epoch on a public wharf ledger, each slot anchored to verifiable off-chain resource cost. Every new identity escrows one pearl bond. A falcon auditor re-samples berths and traces control, slashing all pearls in a cluster sharing an operator. A sybil farm must therefore rent N distinct slots at market price and stake N bonds at risk; farm cost exceeds per-identity reward, so faking stays unprofitable.
